paper_title: 1.4 Million Open-Source Distilled Reasoning Dataset to Empower Large   Language Model Training
caption: Distribution of data entries across different task categories. The dataset primarily consists of Math (29.3%), Coding (24.3%), and Information Seeking (22.2%) tasks, followed by Reasoning (10.4%), Planning (2.3%), Creative Writing (2.2%), and other combined categories (9.3%).
model_annotation: The pie chart illustrates the distribution of data entries across various task categories in a 1.4 million open-source distilled reasoning dataset, with each segment labeled by its corresponding category and percentage. The largest segment, colored red, represents Math, accounting for 29.3% of the dataset. The second-largest segment, in blue, corresponds to Coding, making up 24.3%. Information Seeking, shown in light green, comprises 22.2%. Reasoning, depicted in orange, contributes 10.4%. Smaller segments include Planning (2.3%, light purple), Creative Writing (2.2%, pink), and a combined category for others (9.3%, light green), which includes the remaining tasks. A legend on the left side of the chart provides a key to the color-coded categories and their respective counts, with Math having 410,756 entries, Coding 339,907, Information Seeking 311,427, Reasoning 145,329, Planning 31,757, Creative Writing 30,144, and Others (combined) 130,671. The chart is titled "Distribution of Different Categories" and visually emphasizes the dominance of Math, Coding, and Information Seeking tasks in the dataset.
